companyDescription: AI cloud / GPU infrastructure (pivoted from Bitcoin mining) · Microsoft + Nvidia partnerships, $4B+ ARR target · down 46% from its 52-week high on neocloud-demand fears despite a fresh $2.8B contract win
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Up 2.71% Jul 21, but still down ~46% from the 52-week high ($76.87) after a month-long neocloud selloff (IREN, Nebius, CoreWeave all fell 13-37% in mid-July on Meta-compute-competition fears) that has now started to reverse on fresh contract news.
summary: IREN just signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI cloud contracts (Jul 20, 2026), raising its year-end AI Cloud ARR target to $4B+ (from $3.7B) with ~85% of that now under contract — the stock popped 21% on the news but is still down ~46% from its 52-week high after the broader neocloud sector (IREN, Nebius, CoreWeave) sold off 13-37% in mid-July on fears that Meta reselling excess compute capacity threatens the AI-cloud business model. Next earnings is Aug 27, 2026. 13-16 analysts average $76-81 (+84-96% from here), with Bernstein at $100 (+142%). The bear case is real too: an $800M founder equity package raises dilution concerns, and short interest sits at 21%+. This is a volatile, contract-driven AI-infrastructure name — buy the demand story, size for the volatility.

catalysts.name: $2.8B AI Cloud Contract Signing
catalysts.description: IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year cloud services contracts (announced Jul 20, 2026), lifting its year-end AI Cloud ARR target to $4B+ from $3.7B, with customers now including Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, Figure AI, Together AI, and others — ~85% of the new ARR target is already under contract.

catalysts.name: Q4 FY26 Earnings
catalysts.description: Next scheduled earnings report, where the market will look for the new $2.8B in contracts to start showing up in guidance and for management to address the $800M founder equity dilution concern that's been weighing on the stock.

catalysts.name: Nvidia/Microsoft Blackwell Deployment Ramp
catalysts.description: Continued buildout of the 5-gigawatt strategic partnership with Nvidia (originally a $3.4B contract for a five-year Blackwell GPU deployment) — ongoing capacity coming online is the underlying driver behind the ARR targets.

risks: The $800M founder equity compensation package approved by the board carries real dilution risk for existing shareholders — a genuine overhang, not just noise

Sector-wide neocloud fear is real: Meta's push to resell excess AI computing capacity triggered a 13-37% selloff across IREN, Nebius, and CoreWeave in mid-July, and that structural competitive risk hasn't gone away just because IREN posted a strong contract week
High short interest (21%+) signals real, funded bear conviction about the neocloud business model's durability, not just momentum trading
Debt load is rising across the sector to fund GPU buildouts — IREN's own debt has climbed to over $3.6B, a capital-intensity risk if AI-cloud demand growth disappoints

Customer concentration: a handful of large AI-lab contracts (Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, Figure AI) drive the ARR target — losing or not renewing even one is a bigger swing factor than for a diversified cloud provider

estimateDates.note: Market wants to see the $2.8B in new contracts flow into guidance and clarity on the dilution overhang
estimateDates.est: ARR trajectory toward $4B+ target is the key metric

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, but new Chair Warsh's hawkish tone has 9 of 18 officials projecting a further 2026 hike, with the next FOMC decision Jul 28–29, 2026 — just days after this report.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target and the 10-year yield sits near 4.48%; the early-July AI-chip valuation selloff (Micron -13%, Intel -9%, AMD -7% at points) shows how quickly rate/valuation fears can hit the whole AI-infrastructure complex.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: IREN is capital-intensive, debt-funded, and pre-durable-profitability — among the most rate-sensitive names in this screen. Higher-for-longer directly raises the cost of the GPU buildout funding its ARR growth.
macroRisk.summary: HIGH — this is the most macro-sensitive pick in this screen: a capital-intensive, debt-funded AI-infrastructure buildout is exactly the kind of name a hawkish Jul 28-29 FOMC surprise or a renewed AI-valuation selloff would hit hardest, on top of the sector's own neocloud-competition overhang.
